subject: history_social
notes: The cog was the main type of cargo ship used by merchants of the Hanseatic League, a network of trading towns in northern Europe.
Cogs had flat bottoms, high sides, and a single square sail.
Historians knew about cogs mainly from images on town seals and from written records.
In 1962, workers dredging the Weser River in Bremen, Germany, uncovered the remains of a cog.
Tree-ring dating showed that the ship was built around 1380.
The Bremen cog is among the best-preserved cogs ever found.
stem: The student wants to explain why the 1962 discovery was valuable to historians. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Cogs, the main cargo ships of the Hanseatic League's network of trading towns in northern Europe, had flat bottoms, high sides, and a single square sail.
choices.B: Historians, who had known cogs mainly from town seals and written records, gained a well-preserved example in the Bremen cog of 1962.
choices.C: In 1962, workers dredging the Weser River in Bremen uncovered the remains of a cog that was built around 1380.
choices.D: The Hanseatic League, a network of trading towns in northern Europe, relied on cogs as the main type of cargo ship.

explanation.why: To show why the find was valuable, a sentence must contrast what historians had before (images on seals and written records) with what the discovery gave them (a well-preserved actual ship). Only one choice makes that comparison.
explanation.A: Incorrect. It describes what cogs looked like but says nothing about the discovery.
explanation.B: Correct. It shows that the find gave historians an actual, well-preserved ship where before they had only seals and records.
explanation.C: Incorrect. It reports the discovery accurately but does not explain why it mattered. This is the closest near miss.
explanation.D: Incorrect. It explains what cogs were used for but does not mention the discovery.
